title: The Woman in the Photograph
content:
The trouble began on Monday morning.

Lila was making coffee when Darius appeared at her back door, looking unusually distracted.

“Morning,” she said. “You look like someone cancelled your favorite restaurant.”

“Can we talk?”

Her stomach tightened.

“Of course.”

He stepped inside but didn't sit down.

“I should have told you more about my previous relationship.”

Lila set the coffee pot aside.

“You mean your fiancée.”

He nodded.

“I understand why you're upset.”

“I'm not upset that you had a life before me, Darius. I'm upset that I'm learning about it in pieces.”

“You're right.”

His willingness to accept responsibility disarmed her, but it didn't erase the uneasiness.

“What happened to her?”

“She stayed in the city.”

“Does she know you're here?”

“Yes.”

Lila's fingers tightened around her mug.

“Does she know about me?”

Darius hesitated.

It was only a second, but it was enough.

“Darius.”

“She called yesterday. I told her I'd met someone.”

“Someone?”

“You.”

“Did you tell her you were sleeping with someone?”

His jaw tightened.

“I don't think we need to describe our private life to my ex.”

“No, but I do think you need to be honest with me about whether she's still part of yours.”

He looked at her for a long moment.

“She wants to meet and talk about what happened. I haven't agreed.”

Lila felt the first sharp edge of jealousy.

She hated it. She hated that a woman she had never met could suddenly make her question every moment she had spent with Darius.

“Do you want to see her?”

“I want closure.”

“And what if she wants something else?”

“I can't control what she wants.”

“But you can control what you do.”

He nodded slowly.

“You're right.”

She wished he would argue. It would have been easier to be angry with him if he had been defensive.

Instead, he reached for her hand, then stopped before touching it.

“I don't want to lose what we're building.”

Lila looked at him.

“Then don't make me feel like I'm competing with a ghost.”

“I won't.”

She wanted to believe him.

But that evening, while Darius was out, Lila received a message from an unknown number.

You must be Lila. I'm Vanessa, Darius's former fiancée. I think we should talk.

Lila stared at the screen.

Before she could respond, another message arrived.

There's something about Darius you should know.

Her pulse quickened.

She typed a reply, deleted it, then tried again.

What is it?

The response came almost immediately.

He hasn't told you the whole truth about why he left the city.

Lila felt the room grow strangely quiet.

She wanted to call Darius. She wanted to demand an explanation. Instead, she stared at the message until her phone dimmed in her hand.

Then another notification appeared.

A photograph.

Darius stood beside Vanessa at what looked like an engagement party, his arm around her waist, both of them smiling at the camera.

On the back of the photograph, visible in the image, was a date from only two months earlier.

Lila's heart began to pound.

Two months.

Darius had told her the engagement ended six months ago.

She read the message again.

Ask him why he came here so suddenly.

The front door opened.

“Lila?”

Darius's voice carried down the hallway.

She stood in the kitchen, phone in hand, watching him walk toward her.

His smile faded when he saw her expression.

“What happened?”

She turned the screen toward him.

For the first time since she'd met him, Darius looked genuinely afraid.

“Lila, let me explain.”

She swallowed.

“Tell me the truth.”

He looked at the photograph.

Then he closed his eyes.

And when he opened them again, the man standing in front of her seemed suddenly unfamiliar.
